item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
‘It’s a Wonderful Life, (1946), celluloid film.
…until he finds a room which is painted green…

It's a black and white film.

The Master drops onto his knees and begins praying at a corner of the room outside the purview of the camera. Just before the screen fades to black the area around the Master darkens as if by a negative spotlight and he cries "It's just as I expected!" before falling to one side, blood streaming from his eyes and nose as the film fades to credits.

If you can't see it, how do you know that he's in a corner? (I assume you could hear the praying.)
Also, "purview" isn't actually correct. It generally refers to control and/or understanding, not literal vision.

Upvoted, because this has great potential.
